title: Field-model branch of regularity after purely inseparable base change
statement: The corresponding model branch implies regularity of the finite purely inseparable tensor product of the generic formal fibre.

proof.text: Split by CharP.char_is_prime_or_zero applied to ringChar k. If ringChar k is zero, transfer characteristic zero through the injective constant-series map and the inverse model equivalence, then use the following three steps.

Localize the regular local ring A at P using IsRegularLocalRing.localization_at_prime_and_isRegularRing, apply AdicCompletion.isRegularLocalRing_iff to its maximal-ideal completion C, and apply the regular-local localization theorem again to see that C is a regular ring.

The canonical residue field at the zero prime of the domain A is its fraction field, a localization at the nonzero elements. Mathlib IsLocalization.tensorRight identifies its tensor product with C as the localization of C at their images. At each prime of the canonical localization, Mathlib localizationLocalizationAtPrimeIsoLocalization identifies its local ring with a prime localization of C. Transport regular localness, apply isRegularRing_iff, and use IsLocalization.algEquiv to conclude regularity of the generic formal fibre.

In characteristic zero the fraction field has characteristic zero by IsFractionRing.charZero_of_isFractionRing. A purely inseparable extension of this field has bijective structure map by Mathlib IsPurelyInseparable.bijective_algebraMap_of_isSeparable. Hence TensorProduct.includeRight is bijective; AlgEquiv.ofBijective and IsRegularRing.of_ringEquiv transport the regularity just proved to the required tensor product.

In positive characteristic apply MvPowerSeries.formalFiber_polynomial_isGeometricallyRegular with n=d and m=0. Compose the given model equivalence with the inverse empty-variable polynomial-ring equivalence and take Q to be the inverse image of P under its inverse. The identity P=Q.comap E follows from the inverse identities.

Mathlib Localization.localRingEquiv transports P to Q and map_ringEquiv_maximalIdeal identifies the maximal ideals. Apply AdicCompletion.exists_ringEquiv to get the compatible completion equivalence. Ideal.residueFieldRingEquiv identifies the zero-prime residue fields. The explicit semilinear tensor equivalence sends a tensor x⊗c to the tensor of the two images. Its multiplication law is proved by tensor induction, and compatibility with the residue-field action follows from the pure tensor at 1. Apply Algebra.isGeometricallyRegular_of_fieldIso to the inverse equivalences, then take the purely inseparable regularity component at k'.

proof_origin.place: Proposition Tag 07PS, last two paragraphs; Lemma Tag 07PR with no polynomial variables, plus explicit transport along the model equivalence

lean.statement:
theorem isRegular_genericFormalFiber_fieldModel
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsRegularLocalRing A]
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (d : ℕ)
    (e : Nonempty (A ≃+* MvPowerSeries (Fin d) k))
    (P : Ideal A) [P.IsPrime]
    (k' : Type (max u u)) [Field k']
    [Algebra ((⊥ : Ideal A).ResidueField) k']
    [Module.Finite ((⊥ : Ideal A).ResidueField) k']
    [IsPurelyInseparable ((⊥ : Ideal A).ResidueField) k'] :
    IsRegularRing
      (TensorProduct ((⊥ : Ideal A).ResidueField) k'
        ((⊥ : Ideal A).Fiber
          (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime P))
            (Localization.AtPrime P))))
